headings.title: SMTO-SKL-0140 — The Slack file didn't match its saved copy

html:
SMTO-SKL-0140 — The Slack file didn't match its saved copy

GUID: 11121ae5-b4c7-5585-ae73-31c848f7c49f
Slug: slack-file-integrity-failed
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • SMTO checks every file it moves to or from Slack. This file's contents didn't match what was expected, so SMTO stopped. Nothing was sent to Slack, and no partial download was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you were sending a file to Slack, ask the Agent to create or save the file again in this conversation, then upload the new copy. The saved file changed after SMTO recorded it, so a fresh copy gives SMTO contents it can check.
  2. If you were downloading a file from Slack, ask the Agent to download the same file again. The earlier download ended early or was cut short, and SMTO threw that incomplete copy away.
  3. If the download keeps failing, open the file in Slack and make sure it still opens there and hasn't been replaced or deleted. A file that was replaced or removed in Slack can't be downloaded in full, so the sizes never match.

What success looks like

  • The upload appears once in the Slack channel, or the downloaded file appears in the conversation with no error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or your Slack connection. Don't edit the saved file by hand to make it fit; create a fresh copy instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Slack file transfer stopped because the upload source's size or SHA-256 no longer matches its registered artifact record, or a completed download's byte count differs from the size Slack reported.

What this means

  • Upload-source size/SHA-256 differs from registered metadata, or completed download byte count differs from expected size. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Upload-source size/SHA-256 differs from registered metadata, or completed download byte count differs from expected size.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare exact artifact revision/hash or Slack file size.

How to fix it

  • For uploads, the artifact bytes changed after registration (size_bytes/sha256 mismatch in files.source); regenerate or re-register the artifact and upload the new reference. For downloads, the stream ended with fewer bytes than files.info size; fetch fresh file metadata with slack.file_info and download again, never using a partial transfer.
  • Recreate the source artifact or fetch fresh file metadata; do not use a partial or hash-mismatched transfer.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Integrity is established before the file is published or uploaded.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
